hook: FBI case file section covering August 1952 civilian flying saucer reports, including a sighting at the Savannah River AEC nuclear plant by Du Pont employees, J. Edgar Hoover's standardized forwarding letters to Air Force Intelligence, and a translated anonymous German letter claiming flying saucers were Russian-controlled V-weapons capable of carrying atomic bombs.
why_it_matters: This section documents the FBI's operational role as a passive intake and routing bureau for public UAP reports during the peak 1952 wave, systematically forwarding civilian accounts to the Air Force Inspector General while explicitly disclaiming further investigation. The Savannah River Plant sighting is significant because it places an unidentified aerial object over an active AEC nuclear production facility, consistent with a documented pattern of UAP activity near nuclear sites. The translated German letter introducing a Soviet V-weapon theory with specific technical parameters illustrates the range of foreign-origin intelligence fragments the FBI was processing during this period.
key_findings: Two E.I. Du Pont Company employees observed a 'blue light with an orange fringe shaped like a saucer' flying at high speed in a northeastern direction over the Four Hundred Area of the Savannah River Plant (AEC facility) at approximately 9:30 PM on August 8, 1952.

J. Edgar Hoover signed standardized acknowledgment letters directing at least five civilian reporters (in Wisconsin, Indiana, Michigan, New York, and West Virginia) to the Air Force Inspector General at the Pentagon, with the FBI explicitly stating 'no further action is contemplated in this matter by this Bureau.'

An anonymous German-language letter submitted through the Cincinnati office (translated by the FBI's Cryptanalysis-Translation Section) claimed flying saucers were a V-weapon tested in 1944, disk-shaped with a ~48-50 meter diameter, equipped with 45-50 nozzles around a plexiglass control sphere, capable of carrying atom bombs, 'in Russian hands,' with a claimed range of 30-35,000 km — attributed to V-weapon engineer 'Riedel.'

The Seattle FBI office documented its standing protocol of immediately disseminating all unusual aerial and maritime sighting reports to DIO (Naval Intelligence), OSI USAF, and R-3 Army Intelligence without prior evaluation, serving as a regional coordinator across Oregon and Washington.

OSI District Commander Colonel S.W. Raynor at Wright-Patterson Field told the Seattle office that OSI had 'no interest whatsoever' in flying saucer reports, that Air Force data was correlated at Wright-Patterson in a 'routine fashion,' and that OSI gave 'no credence whatsoever' to the phenomenon, viewing public releases as creating 'mass hysteria.'

legacy_program_connections.reasoning: Wright-Patterson Field is explicitly named as the Air Force evaluation and data correlation center for UFO reports, and OSI District Commander Raynor is quoted directly on how the Air Force handled the data there.

The most operationally significant sighting in this section occurred directly over the Savannah River Plant, an active Atomic Energy Commission nuclear production facility, reported by Du Pont contract employees.

The Air Force evaluation infrastructure at Wright-Patterson described by Col. Raynor corresponds to the Project Blue Book-era centralized assessment structure that received forwarded FBI reports during this period.

The FBI's Domestic Intelligence Division was flagged for review of the translated German letter with a suggestion to share with 'other Governmental Agencies,' implying potential intelligence community routing beyond the Air Force.
